errors.description: The pocket is far too small in the frame. Measured on the 880x1168 candidate: pocket spans x 385-627 (27.5% of frame width) and y 603-876 (23% of frame height), roughly 6% of frame area. The shot includes the model's chin, full collar and most of the shoulder, so it reads as a chest portrait rather than a pocket document. Attempt 2 of this same option frames the pocket at 44% of frame width and does meet the floor.
errors.expected: Chest pocket fills 40-80% of the frame, framed tight on the left chest pocket
errors.actual: Pocket spans 27.5% of frame width / 23% of frame height, about 6% of frame area

errors.description: The V at the pocket base is cut deeper and sharper than drawn. In the illustration the two angled bottom edges drop about 15% of the pocket width to the apex, roughly 17 degrees below horizontal. In the photograph they drop about 20% of the pocket width, roughly 22 degrees. The option still reads unmistakably as the triangle pocket.
errors.expected: Bottom edges angled ~17 degrees below horizontal; apex depth ~15% of pocket width
errors.actual: Bottom edges angled ~22 degrees; apex depth ~20% of pocket width

errors.description: The apex of the V sits slightly left of the pocket's horizontal centre, offset by roughly 3% of the pocket width. In the drawing the point is centred.
errors.expected: V apex centred on the pocket's vertical centreline
errors.actual: Apex offset ~3% of pocket width to the left

errors.description: The placket buttons carry dark grey/black speckles in their thread holes that do not read as clean mother-of-pearl. Not on the showcased feature, but visible at full resolution and inconsistent with the luxury standard.
errors.expected: Clean white/pearl buttons consistent with a premium white dress shirt
errors.actual: Buttons show dark speckle artifacts in the thread holes

single patch pocket on the wearer's left chest, on the pocket side of the button placket exactly as drawn
real photograph on a male model, white cotton poplin, no line-art or CGI look

notes: Attempt 3 of 3, graded against public/images/pocket/triangle-pocket.jpg magnified 6x. The drawn feature itself is reproduced correctly and is instantly recognisable - the failure is framing, not geometry. IMPORTANT FOR A HUMAN REVIEWER: attempt 2 (candidate-2.png) is the better picture overall. It frames the pocket at 44% of frame width, which clears the 40% composition floor that sank attempt 3, and its buttons render cleanly. Attempt 2's V is slightly deeper than attempt 3's (~25% vs ~20% of pocket width against a drawn ~15%), so it trades a small geometry regression for a large composition gain. This is the oscillation-not-convergence pattern; recommend a human compare candidate-2 against candidate-3 and adopt candidate-2 if framing is weighted above the V angle.
